record.Description: Number of individual specimens and live birds measured for each species
Number of measured individuals identified as female
Number of measured individuals identified as male
Number of unsexed individuals measured
Number of measured individuals with complete set of morphometric trait measurements
Length from the anterior edge of the nostrils to the tip of the beak
Width of the beak at the anterior edge of the nostrils
Length from the carpal joint (bend of the wing) to the tip of the longest primary on the unflattened wing

100*DK/Lw, where DK is Kipp’s distance and Lw is wing length (i.e., Kipp’s distance corrected for wing size). Species average HWI differ from estimates in Sheard et al. (2020) because of much higher sampling of individuals in some species, as well as taxonomic effects in the BirdLife list
Body mass given as species average (incorporating both male and female body mass)

NO = all biometric trait data were obtained from direct measurement of specimens, or in the case of body mass from published sources
YES = at least some of the biometric traits were unavailable from specimens so these trait data were inferred from a closely related species; in some cases all morphological measurements were taken directly except for body mass, which can't be measured on museum specimens.

record.Source: Data extracted from primary and secondary literature, particularly Handbook of the Birds of the World (including Birds of the World)

record.Description:
1 = Dense habitats. Species primarily lives in the lower or middle storey of forest, or in dense thickets, dense shrubland etc.
2 = Semi-open habitats. Species primarily lives in open shrubland, scattered bushes, parkland, low dry or deciduous forest, thorn forest. 
3 = Open habitats. Species primarily lives in desert, grassland, open water, low shrubs, rocky habitats, seashores, cities. Also applies to species living mainly on top of forest canopy (i.e. mostly in the open)
record.Source: Tobias et al. (2016) Frontiers Ecol. Evol.

record.Description:
1 = Sedentary. 
2 = Partially migratory, i.e. minority of population migrates long distances, or most of population undergoes short-distance migration, nomadic movements, distinct altitudinal migration, etc.
3 = Migratory, i.e. majority of population undertakes long-distance migration
record.Source: Tobias & Pigot (2019) Phil. Trans. Roy. Soc.

record.Description: Herbivore = species obtaining at least 70% of food resources from plants; Carnivore = species obtaining at least 70% of food resources by consuming live invertebrate or vertebrate animals; Scavenger = species obtaining at least 70% of food resources from carrion or refuse; Omnivore = species obtaining resources from multiple trophic level in roughly equal proportion
record.Source: Pigot et al. (2020) Nature Ecology & Evolution
Pigot et al. (2020) Nature Ecology & Evolution

record.Description: Length from the tip of the beak to the base of the skull
Depth of the beak at the anterior edge of the nostrils
Length of the tarsus from the posterior notch between tibia and tarsus, to the end of the last scale of acrotarsium (at the bend of the foot)
Length from the tip of the first secondary feather to the tip of the longest primary

Length from the carpal joint (bend of the wing) to the tip of the first secondary, i.e. the outermost secondary adjacent to the innermost primary feather. Secondary1 is roughly equivalent to Wing length minus Kipp’s distance (measured in a fully folded and flat wing)
Distance between the tip of the longest rectrix and the point at which the two central rectrices protrude from the skin, typically measured using a ruler inserted between the two central rectrices
